permutationLabel: Acalculous, critically ill (ICU day 9 after polytrauma) — TG18 Grade III
summary: 44-year-old ventilated polytrauma patient on ICU day 9 on parenteral nutrition: new fever 38.9 °C, rising noradrenaline, bilirubin 48, WBC 22; ultrasound shows a distended gallbladder with sludge, 6 mm wall and pericholecystic fluid, no stones.

inputs.chiefComplaint: New fever and rising liver tests in ICU
inputs.hpi: Day 9 in ICU after a road traffic collision (pelvic and femoral fractures, splenectomy day 1). Ventilated and sedated, on parenteral nutrition. Over 24 hours: new fever to 38.9°C, noradrenaline increased from 0.05 to 0.18 µg/kg/min, rising bilirubin and ALP. Lines changed 2 days ago; chest X-ray unchanged; urine clear.

exam.general: Sedated and ventilated. Temperature 38.9°C, pulse 118/min, BP 96/58 on noradrenaline. Mildly jaundiced.
exam.abdomen: Distended; fullness and apparent tenderness (grimace) in the right upper quadrant with a palpable gallbladder. Laparotomy wound clean.

imaging.name: USS abdomen (bedside)
imaging.result: Distended gallbladder (11 cm) with echogenic sludge and no calculi; wall thickened to 6 mm with pericholecystic fluid. No intra- or extrahepatic duct dilatation.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute acalculous cholecystitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute acalculous cholecystitis in a critically ill ICU patient — Tokyo (TG18) Grade III (cardiovascular dysfunction: rising noradrenaline requirement).

mustRankTopK.note: A sedated patient cannot give SOCRATES; the diagnosis rests on fever, a palpable gallbladder and ultrasound.
mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): not in top 3 of ios.bayes: 1. Sepsis | 2. Community-Acquired Pneumonia | 3. Ascending Cholangitis | 4. Bacterial Meningitis / Meningococcal Sepsis | 5. Infective Endocarditis

mustAlarm.note: New fever with a rising vasopressor requirement is septic shock until proven otherwise.

mustInclude.note: Source control in a critically ill patient with acalculous cholecystitis: percutaneous gallbladder drainage.

mustExclude.note: Early LC is not the default for an unstable ventilated patient; an unqualified early-LC line is noise that competes with drainage.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Cholecystitis protocol key points: qualify early LC by grade and fitness (TG18: CCI/ASA-PS; drainage for Grade III/unfit/acalculous critically ill).

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

dxVariant.proposedFix: dx-variants.ts: check Grade III → II → I; add "acalculous" to Grade III keywords when organ dysfunction is documented.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Diagnostic criteria (A local + B systemic + C imaging); Grade II: WBC >18,000/mm³, palpable tender RUQ mass, duration >72 h, marked local inflammation (gangrenous, emphysematous, abscess, biliary peritonitis); Grade III: organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Yokoe M, Hata J, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:41–54.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — flowchart for the management of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Grade I: early LC if CCI ≤5 / ASA-PS ≤2; Grade II: early LC in an advanced centre if fit, otherwise antibiotics and urgent/early gallbladder drainage when not responding; Grade III: organ support, antibiotics, drainage unless favourable organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Okamoto K, Suzuki K, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:55–72.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — management strategies for gallbladder drainage in acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage (PTGBD) as first-line drainage in high-risk surgical patients; acalculous cholecystitis in the critically ill
guideline.citation: Mori Y, Itoi T, Baron TH, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:87–95.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — antimicrobial therapy for acute cholangitis and cholecystitis
guideline.section: Blood cultures in Grade II/III; antimicrobial choice by severity; duration after source control
guideline.citation: Gomi H, Solomkin JS, Schlossberg D, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:3–16.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines 2021
guideline.section: Blood cultures before antimicrobials; antimicrobials within 1 h for shock; source control; noradrenaline first-line vasopressor
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–e1143.

rationale: Permutation: acalculous cholecystitis in the critically ill — no pain history, no stones, septic. Tests that the engines can reach the diagnosis without SOCRATES, recognise sepsis, grade III, and recommend percutaneous drainage rather than an operation.
